item.title: The first time on the street
item.description:
The street as a first time

There is an enormous difference between photographing in your own spaces —home, family, familiar places— and photographing in the street. On the street you control nothing. The light changes, people move, moments pass in a fraction of a second. And the photographer has to decide: move closer or not, shoot or not, wait or keep walking.

This workshop is for anyone who wants to make that first outing with a method. Not improvised, not left to chance: with tools for looking, for moving, and for understanding what happens when you press the shutter.

item.title: Street photography
item.description:
Photographing what happens

Street photography isn’t about photographing people without them noticing. It’s not a surveillance technique. It’s a way of relating to public space: being present, looking, deciding and, sometimes, shooting.

At Llumàtics we’re interested in documentary and street photography as a form of communication — not as a technical exercise. 35mm analogue is the best tool for learning it: it limits you, makes you think, and gives you few shots to waste.
